subject.title: Control UI: Pinned context panel for user-defined persistent facts

question: Should pinned user facts be a first-party Control UI memory feature now, folded into the broader memory-file editor at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46809, or deferred to plugin-contributed Control UI surfaces such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/71736?
rationale: The request changes persistent prompt-influencing user state, and current main only provides raw allowlisted file editing plus read-only workspace browsing, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent storage, injection, UI, and security boundary.

options.title: Keep Canonical Pinned-Facts Design
options.body: Use this issue to settle dedicated pinned-fact storage, always-injected versus last-seen semantics, diff-preview, authorization, and regression proof before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Memory Panel
options.body: Treat the first version as a specialized view in the memory-file editor tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46809 if maintainers want raw memory editing to own the UX.

options.title: Defer To Plugin UI Seam
options.body: Wait for the plugin Control UI contribution-slot direction if maintainers want memory/context panels to be plugin-contributed rather than bespoke core UI.

recommendation.title: Keep Canonical Pinned-Facts Design
recommendation.body: Use this issue to settle dedicated pinned-fact storage, always-injected versus last-seen semantics, diff-preview, authorization, and regression proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses gateway file APIs, workspace/context injection, memory behavior, and plugin-vs-core product direction where the strongest history signal points to steipete.
